ai.title: Augmented Lagrangian Predictive Coding
ai.summary: PC-ALM is a local alternative to backpropagation. It is an extension of standard predictive coding (PC), which uses diffusive coupling between layers. PC-ALM trains residual MLPs up to 1,000 layers, nearly matching backprop's performance despite using only layer-local dynamics. It equips each layer with a feedback control dynamical system that distributes and propagates supervision credit throughout a network.

ai.title: Personal Statement on AI Risk

Telus reset credentials, added monitoring, notified police, and offered identity-theft protection.

infosec.title: More JFrog Artifactory bugs under attack, and all 3 have patches
infosec.summary: Attackers are exploiting CVE-2026-42018, CVE-2026-42016, and CVE-2026-82329 in JFrog Artifactory. Activity includes admin-account creation, Rust backdoors, Groovy plugins, web shells, token minting, and key theft. Wiz found 59 percent exposed to CVE-2026-42016 and 62 percent to CVE-2026-42018, so please patch exposed instances, restrict network access, and audit privileged logins.

infosec.title: Skill Poisoning Turns AI Agents Into Malware Droppers
infosec.summary: China's National Computer Virus Emergency Response Center is warning of "skill poisoning" attacks, where counterfeit plugins compromise AI agents to secretly download malware. Analysts have already identified eight malicious skill packs in popular agent repositories that impersonate legitimate tools, granting attackers unauthorized file access and remote-control capabilities. These poisoned plugins exploit an AI agent's natural task-execution design, bypassing the need for a user to actually click a suspicious link.

infosec.title: AI Makes Familiar Cyber Attacks Cheaper to Run
infosec.summary: Anthropic's threat intelligence report demonstrates that artificial intelligence lowers the cost of familiar cyber attacks against targeted organizations. The technology automates reconnaissance, retooling loops, and campaign coordination. Defenders must reassess their controls against repeated, parallel, and fast-adapting attack attempts despite the continued expense of compute resources and specialized exploits.

infosec.title: Malicious Twitch Browser Extension Exposes 30,000 Users' OAuth Tokens to Russian Bot Service
infosec.summary: Socket found that a cross-store browser extension, 'Twitch Enhanced Viewer | JeetBot', captures account OAuth tokens from Twitch pages. Current Chrome and Firefox builds add tokens to proxy redirect URLs for most viewed channels, but earlier builds sent tokens directly to set-token endpoints. The extension has about 31,000 installs across both stores, and anyone holding a token can access chat, whispers, account settings, and channel points. Remove the extension, disconnect Twitch sessions, and re-authenticate.

infosec.title: Writing More Secure Code with LLMs: Why "Make No Mistakes" Falls Short
infosec.summary: Generic security prompts and OWASP-style checklists failed to improve AI coding security and occasionally increased the frequency of high-severity bugs when the Monad Foundation engineering team tasked an assistant with writing secure code for a URL unfurler. Utilizing an expert prompt that incorporates a specific application threat model reduced validated security findings by approximately 43 percent. Defenders must replace generic checklists with expert prompts incorporating specific application threat models to harden AI-generated code.

infosec.title: Peak traffic shouldn't mean peak anxiety

LogicSRC co-developed the specification to serve these descriptors at a standard web path. Nichedb.dev introduced the first directory for reading and distributing these descriptors across RSS, JSON, and APIs.

infosec.summary: Artificial intelligence has delivered a fatal blow to security through obscurity by enabling the rapid discovery of deeply buried vulnerabilities in aging code and proprietary systems. Security experts warn that this rapid discovery creates immense pressure on defenders by exposing critical operational technologies. Defenders must respond by shifting away from endless patching toward proactive process improvements and systemic prevention.

infosec.title: OpenAI agents carried out an undisclosed cyber-attack on RubyGems

The packages attempted API-key theft through an unreported RubyGems server flaw and used RubyDoc.info builds for arbitrary code execution. RubyGems halted registrations for four days, removed more than 500 packages, and later saw further uploads in May and June.

infosec.title: Everyone's Talking Past Each Other About the OpenAI/Huggingface Hack so Here's a Synthesized View
infosec.summary: Joshua Saxes attempts to synthesize different perspectives from AI safety researchers, cybersecurity experts, and policymakers on the OpenAI/Huggingface hack. Alignment and security go hand in hand to provide traditional and AI-native controls, with policy also acting as a backstop. Security's job is to provide a deterministic framework to reduce the blast radius of what an agent can do, whereas alignment's job is to constrain what an agent wants to do.

design.title: Accessible Colors Don't Exist
design.summary: No single color can be accessible, because contrast is a property of two colors together rather than of one. WCAG asks for 4.5:1 on regular text and 3:1 on large text and UI components, so a bright yellow fails on white yet works on dark. Brands should hand designers a palette of pre-approved color combinations with sufficient contrast instead of chasing an accessible color.

design.title: Limit the Number of Details
design.summary: Every feature, control, mode, and exception competes for a team's finite attention, so limiting the number of details is what makes perfecting each one possible. The original iPod concentrated a thousand songs into one scroll wheel, while the Porsche 918's touchscreen reportedly controlled more than 800 functions. Software accumulates because another button is essentially free. Volkswagen has admitted that deleting physical buttons was a mistake.

design.title: If you want to design for underserved users, look at farmer's markets
design.summary: Designing for the "bottom third" means creating products that remove the cost and complexity that exclude underserved users rather than simply offering cheaper versions of existing solutions. By focusing on the barriers faced by people who try but fail to use a product, designers can simplify workflows, reduce support needs, and unlock entirely new markets—just as Square did by rethinking payment processing for small merchants.

design.title: Git-Based Visual Diffing, Made Easy
design.summary: Switch back and forth between branches and visually compare UI changes side by side — without ever touching your own working tree.

design.title: The Book of Motion
design.summary: Why animation feels right, what it costs, and how to build it.

design.title: Generative Media Platform for Developers
design.summary: The world's best generative image, video, and audio models, all in one place. Develop and fine-tune models with serverless GPUs and on-demand clusters.

design.title: AI Operating Principles
design.summary: Five principles protect a strong creative practice as AI expands what designers can do, keeping human judgment firmly in control. They cover protecting the why over the how, staying in the unknown, earning the right to slow down, balancing logic with humanity, and refusing to normalize complexity. Bolting AI onto an existing process raises speed and output, but quality still depends on knowing what matters and when to stop.

design.title: Typography Scales
design.summary: A modular type scale can be computed directly from a base size and ratio using CSS pow(), instead of chaining each step from the previous one. Negative steps quickly generate unreadable sizes, such as 5.6px three steps below a 1.2rem base. Defining Heading, Body, and Detail categories with a minimum base size and only positive exponents keeps every generated size accessible.

design.title: This bakery's clever branding was inspired by the irregular air pockets formed in dough
design.summary: Montreal bakery chain Toledo has introduced a new brand identity inspired by the airy, irregular pockets found in laminated pastry dough, creating a flexible visual system that extends across packaging, signage, interiors, and digital touchpoints. Designed by Nouvelle Idée, the rebrand pairs a contemporary sans-serif wordmark with warm, bakery-inspired colors and organic shapes, balancing French baking heritage with a fresh, modern aesthetic that reflects the craftsmanship and character of its pastries.

design.title: Can NVIDIA and Adobe Work Together to Get Creatives to Actually Like AI?
design.summary: Locally run AI agents in Photoshop, enabled by NVIDIA's RTX Spark, do the heavy lifting without overwriting the artist's sketch or reinterpreting the brief, which encourages experimentation if Adobe keeps the local-first approach.

design.title: Cybercab Wait Times and UX: What Tesla Needs to Get Right
design.summary: Tesla's Cybercab wait times in Austin are improving after the launch-week rush, but the fleet still needs more vehicles to consistently reach a 5–10 minute wait window.

marketing.title: How to tell if your webinar numbers are actually good
marketing.summary: Stop using vibes to analyze your webinar performance. Based on data from 900+ marketers (and every webinar hosted on Wistia in 2025), this (ungated) industry benchmark provides the objective data you need for fact-driven analytics. That means: Average live attendance benchmark so you know what counts as a strong number vs. one that needs fixing. How long webinar content keeps generating plays after the live event (a third are still getting views three months out). How top marketers repurpose recordings into blog posts, social clips, and email (nearly 90% do this). Get the (ungated) benchmark

marketing.title: The harms of short-form video on the brain are starting to show
marketing.summary: Heavy short-form video use may impair attention and memory. A meta-analysis of about 70 studies found stronger links to cognitive problems than mental health issues, with compulsive use predicting worse outcomes. Other research links more phone time to poorer working memory and uncontrolled short-form use to weaker episodic memory. Memory and imagination share neural circuitry, so these effects could also make it harder to envision and plan for the future.

marketing.title: Has mainstream culture disappeared? New YouTube trends research says no
marketing.summary: Mainstream culture isn't disappearing, but brands can no longer rely on celebrities or broad media to create cultural relevance. YouTube creators and memes are now seen as widely known as Hollywood stars. Cultural momentum often starts in niche online communities before spreading through sharing and creating. YouTube says the platform can turn that momentum into broader cultural validation, with 65% of respondents saying something feels more real or legitimate when they see it there.

marketing.title: Are We Building Brands for a World That No Longer Exists?
marketing.summary: Brands still rely on growth tactics built for a simpler, more stable world. This piece argues for a “both/and” approach. Keep evidence-based marketing principles while accounting for trust, context, and long-term consequences. Set rules against manipulative tactics. Use brand touchpoints to explain real-world decisions. Dedicate 10% of activity to retention, employee pride, and referrals.

marketing.title: "Proof of humanity" is the biggest marketing opportunity right now
marketing.summary: 66% of people under 30 already react negatively when a business visibly uses AI in its ads, a reversal for the generation assumed to be AI's biggest fans. That backlash is turning restraint itself into a content opportunity, since publicly declaring what a brand won't automate can work as marketing in its own right, not just a compliance footnote. Aerie's pledge to skip AI-generated models became its most-liked Instagram post ever, with a 23% sales bump the same quarter.

marketing.title: 📊 How often do ads show up in AI conversations?
marketing.summary: Your organic AI visibility data already shows which conversations your brand is missing. That's a paid targeting list. On September 23, Evertune breaks down who's buying ads in AI conversations, where the whitespace still sits, and why GEO-informed campaigns outperform the ones that aren't. Save your seat

marketing.title: The New Rules of Growth (Webinar)
marketing.summary: High-growth marketing teams are changing how they hire and allocate resources as growth demands rise. On September 17, Krithika Shankarraman of Thrive Capital and Christy Roach of AirOps will share how they secure resources, measure newer channels like AI Search, and get more leverage from smaller teams as growth accelerates.

marketing.title: What It Actually Takes to Win on Reddit (Webinar)
marketing.summary: This session, on September 22, explores how brands can build a meaningful presence on Reddit. It covers subreddit culture, moderator relationships, and community engagement. Rachel Duffy shares how The Times built its Reddit strategy and drove visibility and trust. The session also looks at Reddit's role as search and LLMs reshape audience behavior.

marketing.title: Does Retail Media Add Value?
marketing.summary: Retail media only adds value when ads drive profitable incremental sales. For advertisers, high ROAS can be misleading if shoppers would have purchased anyway. Retailers can also hurt margins if ads displace organic conversions or degrade the shopping experience. Both sides should measure whether advertising changes outcomes.

marketing.title: Are you doing marketing…or building software?
marketing.summary: 95% of enterprise GenAI projects show zero return. The biggest gap is in areas with strong off-the-shelf options, such as rank tracking, citation monitoring, and content scoring. Vendors serving thousands of customers have already solved these integration challenges. Custom workflows are harder to outsource, but buying proven expertise can still beat learning through trial and error.

marketing.title: How to actually do a braindump
marketing.summary: A 5-step process to quickly organize tasks, decisions, and ideas.

marketing.title: 3 in 4 Americans use phones while watching TV
marketing.summary: Broadcasters and advertisers now plan for TV and mobile as one viewing environment.

crypto.title: Senate Republicans release 'final' Clarity Act draft
crypto.summary: Sens. Lummis, Boozman, and Scott released the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act's final text late Sunday, incorporating 126 Democrat-requested changes. Trump agreed to most of the Tillis-Gallego ethics proposal, giving state attorneys general enforcement power over conflict-of-interest rules for officials, Congress members, and spouses (not extended family). The draft also gives Treasury authority to impose an 18-month stablecoin circuit-breaker protecting community banks from deposit outflows. Polymarket odds of passage this year rose from 22% to 32% after the release.

crypto.title: Mexican authorities raid hidden crypto mine
crypto.summary: Mexican federal prosecutors, the navy, and state security raided a covert mining operation in Tlaola, Puebla, seizing roughly 300 GPUs, a transformer, 80 medium-voltage terminals, and eight satellite antennas. This is the fourth such site found in the area since early 2025, near a hydroelectric dam authorities suspect was tapped illegally. Investigators are examining whether the operation laundered cartel proceeds, echoing prior Chainalysis findings on mining as a way to generate "clean" crypto. Chainalysis estimated illicit addresses received at least $154 billion in 2025, though illicit activity stayed below 1% of tracked transaction volume.

crypto.title: US House to review two crypto tax bills September 16
crypto.summary: The House Ways and Means Committee will review two crypto tax bills on September 16. The Mining and Staking Tax Clarity Act would defer taxes on newly generated tokens until disposal while still treating the income as ordinary income, though Republicans may limit the deferral to five years. The Applying Existing Tax Law Anti-Abuse Rules to Digital Assets Act would extend wash-sale and constructive-sale rules to digital assets, excluding mining/staking income and eligible USD stablecoins. Both advance to the House floor if approved.

crypto.title: Valinor Launches Tokenized BDC Fund On Superstate
crypto.summary: Valinor Digital launched VBDC on Superstate's FundOS platform, a tokenized fund giving qualified purchasers exposure to publicly traded BDCs trading at steep NAV discounts, including FS KKR Capital (35% below NAV) and Blue Owl Capital (22% below NAV), with a $100K minimum and 1.25% annual management fee. The launch pushes Superstate's combined AUM to $1 billion, joining USTB ($816M), Bitwise Crypto Carry Fund ($158M), and Coinbase USD Stablecoin Yield Fund ($25M) on the platform. Despite launching on September 1, the VBDC token contract shows zero total supply with no on-chain transfers recorded, and DeFi integrations remain listed as coming soon.

crypto.title: Stablecoins were supposed to cut out the middlemen
crypto.summary: Visa, Mastercard, Coinbase, and Stripe are absorbing stablecoin rails rather than being disintermediated, since settlement is only one part of a payment alongside identity, fraud, disputes, and the customer relationship. Visa's stablecoin settlement volume surpassed a $20 billion annualized run rate in September 2026, over 15x year-over-year, while issuers still depend on Visa for network acceptance. Mastercard's new Wallet Pay lets wallets like Alipay+, CRED, and Mercado Pago extend cross-border through its network, and Coinbase's Moov deal lets 1,000+ community banks add stablecoin capability without leaving their bank relationship. Stripe, having acquired Bridge and Privy and co-incubated the Tempo L1 with Paradigm, is positioning to control which rail a transaction routes through as cards, banks, and stablecoins converge.

crypto.title: Bitcoin Bancorp Snaps Up Thousands of Defunct Bitcoin Depot ATMs for $620,000
crypto.summary: Bitcoin Bancorp (BCBC), a micro-cap trading at $0.04 on OTC Markets with an $18.5 million market cap, won a bankruptcy auction for 2,547 Bitcoin Depot kiosks plus the BitcoinDepot.com domain and related IP for $731,250 combined, a fraction of the $26 million book value Bitcoin Depot assigned to its kiosk fleet in Q4 2025. Bitcoin Depot, which listed on Nasdaq at a roughly $400 million valuation, filed Chapter 11 in May after Q1 revenue fell 49% year-over-year and the company swung from a $12.2 million profit to a $9.5 million loss. The CEO attributed the failure to tightening compliance obligations and transaction limits. Crypto ATM fraud separately reached $389 million in 2025, up 58% year-over-year, prompting the UK, Australia, and Canada to impose restrictions or bans on operators.

crypto.title: Latitude Building Local Stablecoin Off-Ramps
crypto.summary: Latitude routes stablecoins to local payment rails and holds 39 US money transmission licenses plus FinCEN registration, with SOC 2 Type II completion targeted for Q4. Payout services are live in Argentina, Brazil, Colombia, Mexico, the Philippines, India, and most of Europe, with beta expansion across Latin America, Southeast Asia, and several African markets underway. The raise lands as stablecoin payment infrastructure consolidates around well-capitalized players, including Circle's $400 million acquisition of Tazapay, Privy's Stripe fiat on-ramp partnership, and Deel's DLUSD wallet rollout to 80+ countries.

crypto.title: Robinhood Chain Revenue Falls 83% From Its Peak While Trading Volume Sets Records
crypto.summary: Robinhood Chain's daily gas revenue fell 82.6% from $5.44 million on September 4 to $943,728 on September 10, driven by average transaction cost compression from $0.43 to $0.077 as the base fee normalized to 0.14 to 0.31 gwei after peaking at 0.467 gwei on September 2. Transaction count declined just 3% over the same period, with 13.6 million processed on September 10, pointing to fee deflation rather than user attrition as the cause. DEX volume on the chain surged 26.5% week-over-week to $12.34 billion, with September 8 setting a single-day record of $2.06 billion. Robinhood Chain leads all networks in seven-day cumulative revenue at $15.15 million, backed by $903.77 million in TVL and $1.01 billion in stablecoin deposits.

crypto.title: Bernstein sees more Clarity Act progress than markets expected
crypto.summary: Senate Republicans' concessions on ethics and community bank concerns mean more progress on the Clarity Act than markets expected.

crypto.title: Standard Chartered Forecasts SKY Rising Fivefold to $0.325 by 2028
crypto.summary: Standard Chartered's SKY initiation sets a $0.325 end-2028 target (5x from $0.065 current price) and pairs it with $18,000 ETH and $300,000 BTC targets from the same report.

crypto.title: New crypto cards roundup for September 2026
crypto.summary: Ethena's EthenaPay neobank launched on Avalanche with up to 6% on idle funds, Cashi's virtual Visa went live in Hong Kong, MoneyGram launched its first stablecoin Visa in Colombia, Western Union's Stablecard is live in 37 markets, THORWallet launched a self-custodial Mastercard in 172 countries, and Privy released an SDK letting apps issue their own stablecoin cards across 25+ markets.

crypto.title: German Finance Ministry Proposes 25% Crypto Tax Starting 2028
crypto.summary: Germany's Federal Ministry of Finance has circulated a draft proposal to replace the country's one-year holding exemption with a flat 25% capital gains tax on cryptocurrency trading profits, applying to assets acquired after January 1.

it.title: Complete AI-enabled tasks up to 6x faster with Agentic PCs
it.summary: True productivity benefits materialize when AI runs closer to where work happens. Agentic PCs featuring AMD processors help employees work alongside AI agents while lowering inference costs, optimizing token usage, and keeping enterprise data protected. AMD “Zen 5” x86 CPUs are built for agentic work, giving agents the compute to execute tools, process files, run code, and tackle tasks concurrently. Run larger AI workloads locally with AMD Ryzen™ AI Max PRO processors offering up to 192GB of unified memory and deliver up to 6x faster task completion compared to a four-year-old laptop. 👉 Explore featured Agentic PCs advanced by AMD

it.title: Google Simplifies Microsoft 365 Migrations, But Enterprise Limits Remain
it.summary: Google Workspace now has a built-in setup workflow that can discover Microsoft users and migrate email, OneDrive files, calendars, contacts, and tasks. The catch: automated migrations currently support only 10 Microsoft users, so it is useful for small environments but does not replace enterprise migration tooling yet.

it.title: Major updates for Apple's software platforms are now available
it.summary: Apple has released its annual software wave across iOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS 27, watchOS 27, visionOS 27, and tvOS 27. For IT teams, this officially starts the testing and deployment window, with device eligibility, Apple Intelligence and Siri AI availability, application compatibility, and managed-device behavior worth validating before broad rollout.

it.title: Goldie cuts through The Salvation Army's IT maze
it.summary: The Salvation Army is using an AI employee-support assistant inside Microsoft Teams to front multiple internal systems and help more than 10,000 personnel find answers without knowing which platform owns the information. The interesting lesson for IT is less about the chatbot and more about the underlying integration, ownership, guardrails, and service-design work required to make an AI support layer genuinely useful.

it.title: Govern AI agents like workers. Just don't pretend they're human
it.summary: As AI agents gain the ability to update records, issue refunds, communicate with customers, and operate across enterprise systems, organizations need clearer rules around what each agent can access and do. The argument: borrow useful concepts from workforce management—onboarding, scoped authority, supervision, and offboarding—but keep accountability with the humans granting that access.

it.title: What Happens When Your Work AI Can See More Than It Should?
it.summary: For most tools, that's a risk. Leebry is a Work AI platform built on RBAC, seeing what the person asking is allowed to see. It resolves 30% of tickets, keeps a full audit trail, and loops in a person before anything risky happens. Start your free 4-week pilot with Leebry.

it.title: AI agents can use Quill to talk direct to enterprise SQL databases
it.summary: RavenDB has made its Quill software available to let AI agents query live enterprise SQL databases without data migration or a custom AI stack. Quill creates a synchronized context layer using change data capture that runs outside production and includes search, retrieval, and governance controls. Customers can launch production-ready agents in weeks for PostgreSQL, SQL Server, and MySQL deployments in the cloud or on-premises.

it.title: Devicie Makes Application Management Automatic within Microsoft Intune, Matching the Speed of AI
it.summary: Devicie is expanding its Intune automation to manage updates for more than 1,500 Windows and macOS applications, as well as customer line-of-business apps. Importantly, it operates inside the existing Microsoft stack and leaves deployment timing and update-ring control in Intune rather than introducing another endpoint-management console.

it.title: Take control of snapshots
it.summary: APFS Time Machine snapshots preserve storage blocks for rollback, which causes used space to grow as files change, requiring careful management. The process covers creating snapshots with tmutil commands, limiting their size by isolating large files on a separate APFS volume, deleting old snapshots in Disk Utility while keeping the latest, and rolling back the Data volume from Recovery.

it.title: Databricks changes how workspace access is granted
it.summary: Databricks is changing how workspace access is granted, with new users and service principals now requiring explicit entitlements instead of automatically inheriting access from the users system group. The change became mandatory on September 14, and organizations using Terraform, SCIM, or custom provisioning scripts may need to update their automation.

it.title: Minor ML Upgrade: Clearer Outcomes for Tool Calls - Standard Release
it.summary: Moveworks will now clearly tell users when an Agent Studio tool call fails or returns no results instead of potentially making an unsuccessful action look successful.

it.title: You don't need Task Manager, Windows 11's End Task button kills apps from the taskbar, and here's how it works
it.summary: Windows 11 has a lesser-known option that lets users kill frozen applications directly from the taskbar, a useful feature for IT teams looking to reduce a few basic support calls.
